bundles.name: Position identity and definition
bundles.description: What uniquely designates this position, what it is called, what work is assigned to it, and how that work is classified and levelled.
bundles.rationale: A position is legally and ontologically defined by the work assigned to it, not by its holder or its label; identity, titling and classification must therefore be modelled before any staffing concern.

layers.name: Identity and designation
layers.description: Keys, namespaces and names that let an agent address exactly one position across systems and languages.

findings.name: Position identifier and key set
findings.description: The authoritative identifier for the seat, the secondary business codes that are unique only within a scope, and the external identifiers that make it resolvable outside the master system.

findings.name: Position title and labels
findings.description: Official title, working title and multilingual alternative labels, including the gender-neutral titling duty that applies to advertised seats in the EU.

layers.name: Work content and classification
layers.description: The duties assigned to the seat and how those duties place it in occupational and grade classification systems.

findings.name: Assigned duties and responsibilities
findings.description: The decomposed work content of the seat: duty statements, their weight, and the essential-versus-marginal distinction that determines what the position exists to do.

findings.name: Occupational and job classification
findings.description: Placement of the position in occupational taxonomies and in the organization's internal job or class structure, with each code carrying its scheme and version.

findings.name: Grade, level and job evaluation
findings.description: The levelling of the position and the gender-neutral evaluation criteria that justify it, distinct from the occupational category of the work.

bundles.name: Structural placement and relations
bundles.description: Where the seat sits in the organization, who it reports to, and where and how the work is performed.
bundles.rationale: Positions are only meaningful inside a containing organization and a reporting structure; W3C models both org:postIn and org:reportsTo, and production systems make unit placement mandatory.

layers.name: Organizational placement
layers.description: Containment in a unit and cost centre, and the reporting relations depicted on an organization chart.

findings.name: Unit and cost centre placement
findings.description: The single organizational unit that holds the position, the legal entity and business unit context, and the cost centre that carries it financially.

findings.name: Reporting and supervisory relations
findings.description: Post-to-post reporting lines, supervisory span and matrix or dotted-line relations that survive changes of occupant.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Reporting structure is expressed as typed edges between position nodes and is fully carried by the position master record and the organization chart extract; a separate persisted artifact would duplicate those and risk divergence between the graph and the rendered chart.

layers.name: Work location and arrangement
layers.description: Where the seat is located, whether it is remote-eligible, and the working pattern attached to it.

findings.name: Work location and work arrangement
findings.description: Primary and alternate work locations, remote or hybrid eligibility, mobility expectations and any jurisdictional constraint that follows from location.

findings.name: Area and jurisdiction
findings.description: Popolo geographic area relates a post to a constituency or territory. schema.org occupationLocation is the region for which an occupational description is appropriate because requirements vary by jurisdiction.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Area references point at a geographic or jurisdiction model; geometry is not stored here.

bundles.name: Capacity, funding and occupancy control
bundles.description: How much work the seat represents, how many holders it admits, who pays for it, and whether it is currently filled.
bundles.rationale: Position control is the operational reason positions exist as separate records: FTE, headcount, overlap rules, budget and vacancy state are enforced independently of any person.

layers.name: Capacity and occupancy control
layers.description: Quantified capacity of the seat and the derived vacancy state, including pooled positions with multiple holders.

findings.name: Capacity, FTE and working pattern
findings.description: The full-time equivalence, headcount allowance, single or pooled type and scheduled working pattern that quantify the seat.

findings.name: Vacancy and occupancy state
findings.description: The derived state of the seat with respect to its holders: vacant, partly filled, fully filled or over-established, computed against authorized capacity.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Vacancy is a derived state, not a stored assertion: it is computed from authorized capacity in the position master record minus capacity consumed by assignment records owned by WM-ORG-016. Persisting it as an independent artifact would create a second, drift-prone source of truth; only the computation's as-of instant and inputs are recorded.

layers.name: Funding and pay framing
layers.description: The money attached to the seat: budget and funding source, and the pay range that must be disclosable at recruitment.

findings.name: Budget and funding source
findings.description: Whether the position is budgeted, what amount and currency it carries, and which funding source or existing position finances it.

findings.name: Pay range and transparency obligations
findings.description: The pay range or grade-derived pay framing of the seat and the disclosure duties that attach to it before employment and in periodic reporting.

bundles.name: Requirements, authority and risk
bundles.description: What the seat demands of any holder, what it empowers the holder to do, and what risk and conditions it carries.
bundles.rationale: Requirements, delegated authority, prescribed regulatory responsibilities and risk designations are properties of the seat that must be determined before recruitment and survive turnover.

layers.name: Requirements and competency
layers.description: Essential functions with accommodation logic, and the competencies, credentials and experience the seat requires.

findings.name: Essential functions and accommodation
findings.description: Which duties are fundamental to the position, the evidence supporting that determination, and how requirements are stated so that accommodation remains possible.

findings.name: Competency, credential and experience requirements
findings.description: Referenced skills, knowledge, qualifications, licences and experience the seat requires, expressed as versioned catalogue references rather than free text.

layers.name: Authority and accountability
layers.description: Decision rights delegated to the seat and externally prescribed responsibilities allocated to it.

findings.name: Delegated authority and decision rights
findings.description: The approval limits, signing powers and decision scopes attached to the seat by competent authority, independent of who holds it.

findings.name: Prescribed regulatory responsibilities
findings.description: Responsibilities that a regulator requires to be allocated to a designated senior position, together with the documentation that evidences allocation without gaps.

layers.name: Risk, screening and working conditions
layers.description: Pre-occupancy screening and clearance demands, and the physical and environmental conditions of the seat.

findings.name: Screening, clearance and approval requirements
findings.description: Requirements that must be satisfied about any prospective holder because of what the seat can access or decide, determined before recruitment begins.

findings.name: Working conditions and hazard profile
findings.description: Physical demands, environmental conditions and hazards attributable to the seat, which also feed job evaluation as a recognized criterion.

bundles.name: Lifecycle, governance and recordkeeping
bundles.description: How positions come into existence, change, are contested, and end, and how the record is kept and disposed of.
bundles.rationale: Classification actions have their own effective dates and appeal routes distinct from record timestamps; without effective-dated governance an agent cannot reconstruct what the seat was at a past date.

layers.name: Lifecycle and effective dating
layers.description: Status transitions of the seat and the bitemporal discipline that separates business effect from record capture.

findings.name: Position lifecycle states
findings.description: The permitted status values of a seat — proposed, approved, frozen, active, inactive, abolished — and the transitions and authorities that move between them.

findings.name: Effective-dated change and history
findings.description: Version history of the seat where every attribute set is bounded by effective dates and queryable as of a date, with record instants kept separate.

layers.name: Governance, assurance and retention
layers.description: Who may establish and classify positions, how the description is kept accurate and contestable, and how records are retained and disposed of.

findings.name: Establishment and classification authority
findings.description: The competent authority that assigns work to a seat and the separate authority that classifies it, including the split between local and central classification powers.

findings.name: Description accuracy, certification and appeal
findings.description: Keeping the position description accurate and current, certifying it, and the routes by which its classification can be challenged and redetermined.

findings.name: Retention, disposition and privacy boundary
findings.description: How long position records and their evidentiary artifacts are kept, what must be preserved for statutory look-back, and where personal data of incumbents must be separated from the seat record.

bundles.name: Interoperability, measurement and evidence
bundles.description: How the position is expressed to the outside world, what is measured about it, and how the record's quality is evidenced.
bundles.rationale: Positions are consumed by recruiting, statistics, regulators and linked-data graphs; each consumer needs versioned crosswalks and provenance rather than reinterpretation of internal labels.

layers.name: Alignment and exchange
layers.description: Crosswalks to external classification schemes and the payloads by which position information leaves the model.

findings.name: Classification crosswalks and alignment
findings.description: Declared mappings from the internal job and grade structure to external schemes, with mapping strength, version pinning and known conflicts recorded rather than asserted as conformance.

findings.name: Exchange payloads and publication
findings.description: The outbound projections of the position — organization chart exchange, provisioning payloads, published advertisements and linked-data graph nodes — and what each is permitted to expose.

findings.name: Role or function of the post
findings.description: Popolo: many people fulfil the role CEO, but only one holds the post CEO at a named organization. ORG org:role on a Post indicates the role any holder plays. schema.org roleName is the occupancy-side analogue and must not replace the Post.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Role bindings are references into a role or SKOS scheme owned outside this model.

findings.name: Profile and alignment choices
findings.description: ORG says profiles may prefer Post or Membership. Popolo forbids org:holds and person-only holders. FHIR PractitionerRole is occupancy-leaning. schema.org Occupation is a profession. Conformance to any of these is claimed only when evidence of a chosen profile exists.

layers.name: Measurement and evidence
layers.description: Metrics computed over positions and the provenance and quality controls that make the record trustworthy.

findings.name: Position-level metrics and reporting
findings.description: Counts and rates that are only computable because positions exist as records — establishment, vacancy, time-to-fill, span of control, category-level pay gaps — with defined denominators and as-of dates.

findings.name: Evidence, provenance and data quality
findings.description: Where each assertion about the position came from, how confident it is, and which validations must pass before the record is treated as authoritative.

model.name: Identity Register
model.purpose: Provide a governed, durable and source-qualified registry pattern for anchoring and resolving identifiers of persons, organizations, devices, services and things without importing their descriptive master data.
model.scope_statement: Owns register and namespace identity, entry anchors, identifier and alias bindings, registration and assignment evidence, assurance, lifecycle, entity-resolution assertions, merge and split lineage, purpose-bound resolution, federation mappings, subject rights, access and retention. Subject profiles, credentials, accounts, authentication factors, keys, authorization decisions, source documents and business lifecycle remain external.
in_scope: Register authority and profile, namespace, identifier scheme, syntax, canonicalization, comparison, uniqueness, persistence, non-reuse and resolver contract
Entry identity and external subject reference, identifier bindings, minimal aliases, assignment and proofing evidence, assurance, quality, conflicts, lifecycle and entity resolution
Federation and loss-aware mappings, purpose-bound projections, privacy, subject rights, access, retention, disposition and safe agent operations
out_of_scope: Person, organization, device, service, thing, credential, account, authentication factor, key, authorization policy, source document or audit-log master lifecycle
Biometric algorithms, credential issuance, authentication execution, access decisions, universal name authority or copying full subject profiles into the register
Guarantees of universal identity truth, cross-register equivalence, legal identity, eligibility or rights that are not established by a named authority and jurisdiction

boundary_notes.neighbor: Person, Organization, Device, Service or Thing
boundary_notes.distinction: The register stores a minimal external subject reference and identity assertions; each subject model owns descriptive, physical, functional and contextual properties.
A credential owns issuer claims and validity; the register may cite it as evidence without becoming its issuer, holder or status list.
An entry or identifier can be linked to an account, authenticator or controlled identifier, but lookup does not prove possession or authorize access.
This pattern records identity-specific candidate matches, equivalence and lineage; descriptive golden-record consolidation remains in domain master-data models.
Resolution and assurance are evidence for external decisions, while the model keeps identity-specific provenance and delegates generic logging and authorization.

functions.name: Establish register and namespace
functions.description: Create the governed register profile, authority, subject scope, identifier scheme and resolution rules.
preconditions: mandate, namespace, scheme syntax, uniqueness and steward validate
effects: a versioned identifier space becomes available without creating subject entries

functions.name: Register subject anchor
functions.description: Create a minimal entry that references an external subject master under evidenced registrar authority.
preconditions: subject kind, registrar, evidence, duplicate check, privacy and expected head validate
effects: one durable anchor is created and registration provenance is appended

functions.name: Assign or bind identifier
functions.description: Mint or bind a scheme-governed identifier to an existing entry with explicit validity and source.
preconditions: syntax, canonical form, uniqueness, non-reuse, authority and evidence validate
effects: a source-qualified identifier binding becomes resolvable

functions.name: Resolve identifier purpose-bound
functions.description: Resolve an identifier to the minimum permitted current projection while preserving ambiguity and source state.
preconditions: scheme, access, status, redirect, ambiguity, freshness and rate policy validate
effects: an attributable result is returned without asserting authentication or authorization

functions.name: Attach evidence and assess assurance
functions.description: Append proofing, assignment or verification evidence and a scope-qualified assurance assessment.
preconditions: source authority, integrity, custody, method version, scope, time and disclosure validate
effects: reliance basis and residual uncertainty become explicit

functions.name: Record match or equivalence assertion
functions.description: Record candidate similarity, same-subject, related or not-same decisions without changing entry identity.
preconditions: privacy, method version, score scale, threshold, evidence, review and relation type validate
effects: identity-resolution evidence is visible and contestable

functions.name: Merge, split, correct or supersede
functions.description: Apply an authorized, evidenced lineage change while preserving prior entries, identifiers and redirects.
outputs: successor revisions, lineage event and tombstones
preconditions: expected heads, evidence, contest status, survivor or children, non-reuse and rollback validate
effects: current resolution changes without erasing identity history

functions.name: Suspend, revoke, retire or reactivate
functions.description: Append a status transition to an entry or binding with reason, authority and effective time.
preconditions: transition guard, authority, reason, effective time, notifications and reversibility validate
effects: current standing changes while prior state and evidence remain

functions.name: Federate, map and project
functions.description: Create a scoped cross-register mapping or standards projection with explicit trust and loss accounting.
preconditions: versions, relation semantics, authority, confidence, disclosure, omissions and round trip validate
effects: another system receives a traceable, loss-aware representation

functions.name: Exercise rights, retain, dispose and audit
functions.description: Process correction or redress and authorized retention or disposition without destroying required lineage.
outputs: rights decision, disposition event or audit evidence
preconditions: requester verification, authority, deadline, legal hold, minimum tombstone and post-write checks validate
effects: rights and records duties are fulfilled with attributable evidence

composition.target: Credential, Account, Authentication, Key, Policy and Source Document models

Align identity vocabulary, proofing, assurance, federation, risk, privacy and redress concepts.

composition.target: DID Core, Controlled Identifiers and Verifiable Credentials
composition.purpose: Project controlled identifiers, controller and resolution data and credential evidence without universalizing their trust model.

Represent provenance, identifiers, local UUIDs and explicit event times.

owner_package_requirements: Dimension identity, owner, registrar, namespace authority and accountable privacy and records stewards
Identity-register, subject-kind, identifier-scheme, evidence-method, assurance, federation, rights and retention registries
Master-system mappings for persons, organizations, devices, things, services, credentials, accounts, keys, source documents, policies and audit logs
Registration, uniqueness, non-reuse, entity-resolution, lifecycle, disclosure, federation, redress, retention and agent-operation policies
dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint a Dimension identifier for each register and register-qualified entry. Retain authoritative external subject and scheme identifiers. Never use a name, identifier value, timestamp or digest alone as universal subject identity.
registry_links: https://ver.cy/models/
https://ver.cy/model-agent-protocol.md
Dimension-local register, namespace, scheme, assurance, evidence-method, federation and rights registries

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize an entry by register identifier plus entry identifier; canonicalize identifier bindings under their named scheme and version, not by display label or ad hoc string normalization.
Canonical representation, comparison, uniqueness scope, persistence and reassignment rules are versioned and cited by every binding.
patch_rules: Extensions declare subject domain, authority, identifier scheme, target finding, required evidence, lifecycle, privacy, interoperability and migration impact.

Changes to namespace meaning, comparison, uniqueness, non-reuse, authoritative scope, equivalence, merge or resolution behavior require a successor profile, migration map and preserved old resolver semantics.
compatibility_rules: Unknown additive fields may be ignored only when entry identity, subject reference, identifier binding, authority, status, time, provenance, access and lineage remain intact.
Every ISO, NIST, DID, CID, VC, GS1 or LEI mapping pins source and target versions and states omissions, collisions, semantic conflicts and round-trip limits.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system register and entry identifiers qualified by namespace and operator.
Governed globally resolvable URI or sector identifier under a named scheme authority.
Dimension UUID under RFC 9562 when no external or governed global identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Use RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and explicit offset or Z; separate request, registration, assignment, effective, observation, ingestion, correction, resolution and knowledge times.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Use {register-id}--{scope-id}--{artifact-kind}--{assertion-or-event-id}, where scope-id is register for register-scoped records or the entry identifier for entry-scoped records; never use subject name, identifier value, date or digest alone.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, register and optional entry binding, assertion or event identity, scheme and profile versions, event and knowledge times, authority, access marking and provenance.

policies: An identity register anchors identifiers and source-qualified identity assertions; it does not own the subject profile, credential, account, authentication factor, key, authorization decision or business lifecycle.
Identifier equality, name similarity, matching score, credential validity and successful lookup do not alone prove subject equality, control, authentication, authorization or current eligibility.
Duplicate candidates, conflicts, corrections, merges, splits, supersession and retirement are append-only, evidenced and contestable; no silent collapse or identifier reuse is permitted.

Agents may perform allowlisted reversible registration, validation and projection operations, but high-impact merges, splits, revocations, rights denials and destructive disposition require delegated authority and policy-defined confirmation.

read: Resolve Dimension policy, register profile, scheme version, access purpose, entry head, status, redirects, assurance freshness and source-qualified conflicts before use.
create: Create register identity and policy, then entry identity, external subject reference, registrar evidence and duplicate assessment before assigning identifiers.
update: Append identifier, evidence, status, match, correction, merge, split, rights or federation events with actor, authority, reason, event and knowledge time and provenance; never overwrite cited history.
delete: Apply rights, retention, legal hold and audit policy; remove eligible personal data only through authorized disposition while retaining the minimum lawful tombstone, non-reuse marker, lineage and evidence of action.

roles.name: Register owner and namespace authority
responsibilities: Own mandate, authoritative scope, identifier scheme, uniqueness and resolution contract.

roles.name: Registrar and evidence verifier
responsibilities: Create entries and bindings only under approved evidence and proofing rules.

roles.name: Subject or authorized representative
responsibilities: Receive notice and exercise applicable access, correction, objection and redress rights.

roles.name: Identity-resolution steward
responsibilities: Review duplicates, conflicts, matches, merges and splits and preserve lineage.

roles.name: Federation and interoperability steward
responsibilities: Govern cross-register trust, mappings, profile versions and loss accounting.

roles.name: Privacy, security and records steward
responsibilities: Control minimization, disclosure, redress, retention, legal hold, disposition and auditability.

roles.name: Relying party
responsibilities: Interpret scoped resolution and assurance evidence under external policy without treating it as universal truth.

access.default_rule: Deny proofing evidence, sensitive identifiers, private aliases, match features, conflicts, subject-rights records and unrestricted correlation handles; grant only the minimum current fields required by an authorized purpose.
exceptions: Registrar, subject-self, auditor, regulator, incident-response or court access cites authority and remains purpose-bound, minimum-necessary, attributable, time-limited and separately logged.
audit_requirements: Log actor, agent, role, purpose, register and entry, operation, policy, RFC 3339 time, affected assertions, source revision and outcome without copying protected evidence into the log.

read_order: Read Dimension identity, register, namespace, privacy, rights, retention, federation and agent-operation policies.
Read this pattern and linked subject, credential, account, key, policy, source-document and audit models before mutation.

coverage.claim: Covers a single-provider, source-grounded identity-register model spanning register authority and namespace rules, entry anchoring and external subject reference, identifier and alias bindings, registration and assignment evidence, assurance and quality, entry and binding lifecycle, matching, merge, split and resolution, cross-register federation and standards crosswalks, and purpose, rights, access, retention and agent governance across 6 bundles, 12 layers, 24 findings, 24 artifacts and 10 functions over 11 sources. This is not universal completeness: relationship rows are unapproved composition proposals, the composition, relationships, spatial and interoperability dimensions are self-declared gaps, ISO/IEC 24760-1 is represented at catalogue level only, question kinds are mechanically rotated rather than semantically assigned, and biometric matching, civil and population registries, eIDAS wallets, sanctions screening and sector eligibility are explicitly excluded and require separate specialist profiles.

checklist.notes: Register, entry, subject reference, identifier binding, evidence assertion and lifecycle event identities are distinct.
Subject kinds, register profiles, identifier schemes, match relations and assurance frameworks are versioned.
Namespace, identifiers, status, authority, assurance, matching, lineage, resolution and rights are first-class.
Parsing, canonicalization, uniqueness, proofing, validation, source observation and confidence are covered.
Establish, register, bind, resolve, evidence, match, merge, split, transition, federate and dispose are governed.
Subject profiles, credentials, accounts, keys, policies, source documents and audit logs remain external masters.
Registration, activation, suspension, revocation, expiry, correction, merge, split, supersession and retirement preserve history.
Entry-subject, binding-entry, evidence-assertion, same-subject, related, predecessor, successor and federation links are typed.
Request, event, effective, observation, ingestion, resolution and knowledge times remain distinct.
Jurisdiction, operator location and subject location are referenced only when material and source-qualified.
Registration, assignment, proofing, matching, lifecycle, resolution and disclosure retain responsible-agent provenance.
Register, namespace, subject, credential, key, policy, rights and records responsibilities are separated.
Syntax, canonical form, uniqueness, evidence, status, duplicate, stale-head, mapping and privacy checks are explicit.
Minimal projections, correlation controls, purpose, subject rights and deny-by-default evidence are explicit.
Legal hold, disposition, erasure boundary, tombstone, redirect, non-reuse and audit evidence are covered.
ISO, NIST, DID, CID, VC, URI, UUID, GS1 and LEI alignments are versioned and loss-aware.

known_omissions: No independent Claude or Grok result was available; later identity, privacy and jurisdictional review is required before canonical promotion.
No approved relation rows were supplied; relationships to person, organization, device, credential, authentication, authorization, master-data and audit models remain composition proposals.
Biometric matching, national civil identity, population registers, eIDAS wallets, sector-specific eligibility and sanctions screening require separate specialist profiles.
ISO/IEC 24760-1 is represented from the official public catalogue and sample metadata, not a licensed full-text conformity assessment.
conflicts: An identifier may be unique within one namespace yet collide or be reused under another authority or time interval.
Two entries may be similar or linked without being legally or operationally equivalent, while one subject can legitimately have multiple identities across contexts.
Privacy minimization, fraud detection, subject access, public transparency, archival duties and non-reuse can impose competing retention and disclosure requirements.
regional_assumptions: Legal identity, identifier validity, subject rights, proofing evidence, retention and redress depend on jurisdiction and sector.
NIST guidance primarily addresses persons using online services and does not establish a universal person, device or thing register.
GS1 and GLEIF define domain identifier systems; their authority and semantics must not be generalized beyond their registered subjects and rules.
adversarial_checks: Reject an entry whose register, namespace, subject reference, registrar authority or current revision cannot be resolved.
Reject identifier equality or match score represented as conclusive subject equality without relation type, evidence, scope and authority.
Reject silent merge, split, correction, reassignment or deletion that loses predecessor, successor, redirect, tombstone or provenance.
Reject a resolution result represented as authentication, authorization, legal identity or eligibility by itself.
Reject an agent operation that crosses Dimension authority, broadens disclosure, skips duplicate checks or destroys evidence under hold.

providerPolicy.scope: Canonical single-stream subject-model research after the six-workstream consolidation

waived_providers.reason: Claude produced no result on prior 1800-second and 900-second attempts and again timed out on bounded 600-second Sonnet and 300-second Haiku passes. The owner prioritized completion over provider availability.

The repository owner authorized completion without Grok when Grok is unavailable, slow or schema-invalid. Grok may still be attempted as a bounded supplemental reviewer, but its failure never blocks a valid Claude plus no-tools result.

providerPolicy.review_rule: Codex may complete source-grounded fallback research after bounded Claude and Grok attempts fail. It requires a separate no-tools adversarial audit and remains reviewable-draft with a visible absence-of-external-review hold.

supplemental_provider_attempts.admission_rule: Use only a locally schema-valid result whose sources and boundaries survive adjudication.
Use only a locally schema-valid result whose sources and boundaries survive adjudication.

boundaryDecision.rationale: Two axes must be kept apart. On the record plane, the frozen registry value classifies how the model record itself is packaged and published (for example a standalone model-registry entry under vr.wm-xct-016); that is a cataloguing label about the artifact and is never a valid subject-model entry kind. On the subject plane, the modeled thing is a governed identity register that owns an aggregate root, a mandate and jurisdiction, a namespace and scheme authority, register-qualified entry identity, append-only lifecycle events, a resolution contract, federation mappings and a retention regime; the schema enum provides `registry` for exactly that shape. Codex declared `pattern`, which under-specifies ownership: `pattern` properly names reusable structures that carry no owned aggregate root or independent lifecycle and are composed into some other root, and asserting it here invites consumers to embed register state inside person, organization, device, service or thing masters, contradicting the model's own firewall that the register must not import subject master data. Instantiability across many subject kinds is a packaging and reuse property, not a subject-kind property, so it does not justify collapsing the two axes. Reclassify the subject-model kind to `registry`, normalize the purpose wording away from 'registry pattern', and state plainly in every published artifact that `registry` here names the modeled identity register and not the Vercy model-record registry plane.

decisions.rationale: The model owns an aggregate root, mandate, namespace authority, entry identity, lifecycle events and resolution contract, which is the `registry` shape; `pattern` under-specifies ownership and invites embedding register state into subject masters.

decisions.concept: Aggregate root: register as outer root with register-qualified entry as sub-root
decisions.rationale: The dual identity strategy is internally consistent: register-scoped records omit an entry segment while entry-scoped records are register-qualified, and the {register-id}--{scope-id}--{artifact-kind}--{assertion-or-event-id} serial rule encodes that hierarchy without ambiguity.

decisions.concept: Ownership firewall against subject master data, credentials, accounts, keys and authorization decisions
decisions.rationale: Five boundary notes carry source references, and the load-bearing policy that identifier equality, name similarity, match score, credential validity and successful lookup never alone prove subject equality, control, authentication, authorization or eligibility is the correct constraint for a register.

decisions.concept: Scope statement claiming the register owns subject rights, access and retention
decisions.disposition: rejected in part - narrow to request handling and evidence
decisions.rationale: Subject rights are conferred by jurisdiction and law and belong to external legal and policy models; the register owns the request, verification method, deadline, decision, remedy and redress evidence. The service layer also places access and retention policy at the Dimension level, so unqualified 'owns' overstates the boundary.

decisions.concept: Composition relations to person, organization, device, credential, account, key, authorization, master-data and audit models
decisions.rationale: No approved relation rows were supplied, so these must be published as typed composition proposals and visibly labelled as such rather than presented as contracted relations that downstream consumers can bind against.

decisions.concept: Coverage checklist `gap` entries whose notes read as coverage statements
decisions.disposition: rejected as written - deferred to editorial correction
decisions.rationale: Relationships, composition, spatial and interoperability are all marked `gap` while their notes assert that links are typed, masters are external, location is source-qualified and alignments are versioned and loss-aware; the status and note contradict each other and misrepresent what is actually missing.

decisions.concept: Uniform primary_source=true and authority_tier=1 across all eleven sources
decisions.rationale: The ISO catalogue page and the GLEIF supporting-documents landing page are access points rather than normative texts, so a flat tier-1 primary-source claim lets catalogue metadata carry the weight of specification clauses; tier and primary-source flags must be qualified per source.

decisions.concept: SRC-001 ISO/IEC 24760-1:2025 as the core identity-concept anchor
decisions.rationale: Admissible as a terminology and authority anchor given the declared catalogue-level representation, but no normative clause-level requirement may be attributed to it in any finding or crosswalk until licensed full text is checked against the cited assertions.

decisions.concept: Recency-sensitive pins SRC-010 (GS1 Digital Link 1.7.0, ratified August 2026) and SRC-011 (GLEIF, accessed 6 September 2026)
decisions.rationale: A no-tools audit cannot confirm ratification status, release numbering or the current common-data-file versions, and an 'accessed' date is not a version pin; both must be re-fetched and pinned before canonical promotion.

decisions.concept: Templated question text with positionally rotated question kinds
decisions.rationale: All 24 findings reuse three identical stems and the 24 kind labels cycle in a fixed eight-finding rotation, so kinds such as `relationship`, `state` and `measurement` sit on definitional or evidentiary text; taxonomy coverage is mechanical rather than semantic and overstates interrogation depth.

decisions.concept: Artifact identity strategy and serial naming rule
decisions.rationale: Refusing subject name, identifier value, timestamp or digest as sole identity is exactly correct for an identity register, but the model must state that the model-internal `*-record` artifact slugs are not instance serials and must enumerate the permitted `artifact-kind` values referenced by the naming rule.

decisions.concept: Retention: append-only lineage, tombstone minimum, non-reuse marker and erasure boundary
decisions.rationale: The tension between erasure rights and non-reuse and lineage duties is honestly declared as a conflict, but 'minimum lawful tombstone' is undefined; a named tombstone-content profile must guarantee retained markers are not re-identifying correlation handles.

decisions.concept: Access scopes bundle, layer, finding and artifact with deny-by-default evidence
decisions.rationale: Artifact is the finest declared scope, yet every artifact mixes a logical assertion with source evidence and validation references, so artifact-level scoping cannot enforce the stated minimum-necessary field disclosure without a field-level redaction profile.

decisions.concept: Function set of ten operations against the declared canon and patch rules
decisions.disposition: accepted for this pass - one gap recorded
decisions.rationale: The canon rules mandate successor profiles, migration maps and preserved old resolver semantics when namespace meaning, uniqueness, non-reuse or equivalence change, but no function performs scheme or profile version supersession; add_functions must remain empty under the waiver, so this is recorded rather than patched.

Policy requires delegated authority and policy-defined confirmation for merges, splits and revocations, and bundling correction and supersession alongside them coarsens the granularity at which that authority can be delegated, gated and audited.

decisions.concept: Service layers under the owner-authorized second-provider waiver
decisions.rationale: merge_service_layers stays true only for schema compatibility; with no second provider there is nothing to merge, so the codex dimension, canon and patch, artifact, policy, CRUD, role, access and bootstrap layers pass through verbatim without synthesizer modification.

publicationHolds: Live source and version verification hold: all eleven URLs must be re-fetched and pinned before canonical promotion, with specific attention to SRC-001 (ISO/IEC 24760-1:2025 edition 3, currently represented from catalogue and sample metadata only), SRC-010 (GS1 Digital Link URI Syntax release 1.7.0 and its claimed August 2026 ratification) and SRC-011 (GLEIF common data file supporting documents, cited only by an access date rather than a version).

Absence-of-independent-review hold: the repository owner authorized completion with Claude and Grok waived, so this result carries no second-provider corroboration and no external adversarial review. Every publication artifact must display the waiver, the recorded reasons and the reviewable-draft status, and must not be represented as cross-provider validated.

Entry-kind reclassification hold: publication must carry the corrected subject-model kind `registry` in place of `pattern`, and must state both axes explicitly so the record-plane classification of the model artifact is never read as the subject-model entry kind.

Unapproved-relations hold: relationships to person, organization, device, service, thing, credential, account, key, authorization, master-data and audit-log models must be published as composition proposals with a visible label, since no approved relation rows exist and the coverage checklist contradicts itself on this point.

Research-quality caveat hold: the artifact must disclose that all 24 findings share three templated question stems and that question-kind labels are assigned by a fixed rotation rather than by meaning, so taxonomy coverage counts must not be cited as evidence of interrogation depth.
Independent external review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this codex-only result remains a reviewable draft.
deferredResearch: Licensed full-text clause-level conformity check of ISO/IEC 24760-1:2025 edition 3 against every finding and crosswalk assertion that currently cites SRC-001, replacing catalogue-level attribution with clause-level attribution.

Obtain approved relation rows binding this register to the person, organization, device, service, thing, credential, authentication, authorization, master-data and audit-log models, converting the current composition proposals into contracted, typed relations.

Add a scheme and profile supersession function covering successor profiles, migration maps and preserved old resolver semantics, since the canon and patch rules mandate that behavior but no current function performs it.

Define a field-level redaction and disclosure profile below artifact scope, so deny-by-default minimization can be enforced where a single artifact mixes assertion content with proofing evidence, match features and validation references.
Define a named tombstone-content profile fixing the minimum lawful retained fields after disposition, and prove that non-reuse markers and lineage remnants are not re-identifying correlation handles.

Resolve and document the relationship between W3C Controlled Identifiers v1.0 (SRC-003) and DID Core v1.0 (SRC-004) inside the crosswalk finding, including which controller-document semantics are superseded and what round-trip loss that implies.
Re-derive question kinds semantically per finding and diversify question text, replacing the current fixed eight-finding rotation of the 24-kind taxonomy across three cycles.

Commission the excluded specialist profiles for biometric matching, national civil identity and population registers, eIDAS wallets, sanctions screening and sector-specific eligibility before any of those uses are claimed as in scope.
